attempts.prompt: Use case: identity-preserve. Asset type: one transparent 2D combat idle sprite. Create a NEW full-body SIDE-VIEW pose of the Mannequin Monster from Silent Hill: Revelation (2012). Input image 1 is the project's existing candidate creature and fixes its visual identity: one low spiderlike dark central carapace, pale aged shop-mannequin plastic components, joint sockets, four head-bearing branches and its existing articulated supports ending in mannequin hands or feet. Inputs 2 and 3 are original production-booklet reference pages: use only the creature's grey CGI views and Mr X Rev9/9.1 renders as structural/material reference; do not reproduce people, text or layouts. Rotate the WHOLE creature into a strict broadside profile facing screen RIGHT: its central mouth/front points to the right edge, body axis parallel to the image plane, not toward the viewer. Keep all its appendages, heads, hand tips and foot tips complete and inside the image, far-side supports visible with only natural small offsets. Idle stance: low crouch, supports planted, no attack, no moving limbs, same four head branches as the existing candidate. Preserve sculpted artificial plastic surfaces and dark shell, not flesh or injured people. No new limbs, no new heads, no props, no weapons, no human victim. Composition: one subject in one pose on a wide transparent canvas, the full silhouette occupies the central 65% of width and height, with at least 15% empty transparent border around every extremity. Deliberately zoom OUT so that all appendages fit comfortably. Detailed restrained horror-game raster rendering, neutral diffuse lighting, real transparent RGBA including gaps between limbs, crisp clean edges. No shadows, floor, aura, fog, text, watermark, panels or duplicate figures. This is a candidate versus pose adapted from the evidence, not an original film frame or certified model reconstruction.
attempts.reason: Oblique camera and 7.6 percent horizontal margins. Initial preview raised brown-halo concern; subsequent alpha audit shows off-silhouette low-alpha pixels, so an opaque runtime halo was not established.

Use case: identity-preserve. Create one full-body right-facing COMBAT IDLE cutout sprite of the Lying Figure from the 2026 film Return to Silent Hill. Reference 1 is the project's existing candidate portrait; preserve this specific slender elongated creature, its dark charcoal grey tight continuous wrinkled sheath, sloping enclosed featureless head, constricted upper torso with arms entirely contained inside the sheath, long thin legs, and two small bare feet. Reference 2 is the actual Return to Silent Hill movie still, photo 16: use only the whole creature in the middle as source-specific silhouette evidence, not the environment. It establishes the featureless tapered hood, very narrow waist, arm-contained torso and two separate slim legs. Produce a DISTINCT new pose viewed in strict TRUE 90-DEGREE LATERAL PROFILE facing SCREEN RIGHT, as in a 2D fighting game: side of torso and head visible, chest points exactly to right edge, not toward camera. Quiet tense idle with slightly bent knees, near foot a little ahead, both complete feet visible on the same implied ground line; head inclined forward and upward only as appropriate for the enclosing sheath. No free arms or hands and no new appendages. No weapons, no straps or added clothing, no human face, no chest opening. Restrained detailed horror-game raster rendering under neutral diffuse light, preserving the existing material palette. Entire head, torso, both legs and every toe inside the frame. Center the full body within the middle 65 percent of a square canvas, at least 15 percent EMPTY TRANSPARENT margin above the head and below both soles and generous space on both sides. Real transparent RGBA background, including gap between legs; no floor, no cast shadow, no colored halo, no fog, no scenery, no panels, no text. One subject and one pose only. The unobserved side volume is an explicit candidate reconstruction, not a certified original model. Do not substitute the 2006 Armless or any SH2 game edition.

Use case: game-asset generation from source-specific reference. Create ONE full-body transparent combat-idle sprite of RED PYRAMID from the original SILENT HILL film directed by Christophe Gans, released in 2006. Reference 1 is an actual 2006 film still of this character, and is the controlling reference for the final filmed costume, silhouette, colors, large triangular helmet and long broad Great Knife. Reference 2 is Andy Chung's 2005 final film concept sheet: consult its helmet side view and long costume proportions, but do not copy the sheet, early mechanical ideas, annotations or red paint splashes. The official production notes describe the tall powerful body, skin-like skirt and platform boots; keep the skirt very long so the platforms are mostly concealed, with both complete boot toes and soles visible. Match the filmed 2006 identity: towering lean-muscular pale grey bare torso and long bare arms, no chest harness or shoulder straps, long weathered ochre-brown hide-like apron/skirt from the waist nearly to the ground, dark worn platform boots, large dark rusted pyramidal helmet with its distinctive forward-descending point and ribbed metal panels. The head and all facial features are completely concealed. Do not substitute the SH2 game design, Homecoming, Arcade, Revelation fire scene or Return to Silent Hill design. CAMERA AND POSE: true 90-degree ORTHOGRAPHIC SIDE PROFILE facing screen RIGHT, entire body and helmet turned sideways, chest direction exactly toward right edge, not three-quarter. Calm heavy grounded idle, knees only slightly flexed, two planted feet with a modest stagger on one ground baseline. The near hand grips the Great Knife's complete handle beside the thigh; the huge long broad blade trails down and back to the LEFT with its tip just above the implied ground, entirely visible. Free hand hangs relaxed with complete fingers visible. Full helmet, body, both arms, all fingers, complete long skirt, both boot ends and entire weapon included. One subject and one pose, no opponent or victim. Neutral diffuse lighting and detailed realistic horror-game raster cutout, subdued aged surfaces, no fresh violence or splatter. COMPOSITION: deliberately zoom OUT on a wide transparent canvas, full character plus entire knife contained within the central 65 percent of the canvas, generous 15–18 percent transparent border on all four sides, especially before the blade tip, above the helmet and below the boots. Real RGBA transparency, including gaps around arms and weapon. No scenery, no floor, no cast shadow, no haze, no brown aura, no colored outline, no lettering, no watermark, no panels. Candidate versus adaptation; exact hidden side details are not certified.
